items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: a couple of times Lorenzo Stahl played with us too.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, I met him once. Yeah, Tom Benton.
Where's the other one? Well, a couple of times Lorenzo Stahl played with us too.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Lorenzo Stahl, I'm just putting some stuff in now, Lorenzo Stahl, he was with Jack Carey, he was playing manager.

ctx.x: Robichaux, well anybody around here tell him, he's younger than any of us too. But I do believe he did. We all called him Robichaux, see because I went to his house one time to get him to play. And he said that we should whistle for musicians, like that. So his old mother, somebody come to the door and said, what dog are you calling? I said Robichaux. Boy I point up, I said Robichaux. So he come to the door and say old man, I said yeah I am, I said I'm feeling no mind. So you know it's one of them things you…
Boy he made Robichaux for a boy cry like a baby. That's true for me to God ever. Did you read with those bands like Ernest Johnson? No. Did you read with Jack Carey?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Lorenzo Stahl on guitar, and Bob Lyons on bass. That's how it was.

ctx.x: Well, Chris was a nice man with a plunger, you know. He was a plunger man. Yeah, I know. Well, I'm going to tell you how this happened. When I first came here from the Army, somebody carried me down to 25, where Louis was playing. And I got up there and played two numbers over there and some other song I played. And oh, that's the, let me see what, no, Kid Olive wasn't there. There's Kid Orange, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots, Lorenzo Stahl on guitar, and Bob Lyons on bass. That's how it was. And I played them two tunes…
Well was Louis copying anybody at that time? Did he have his own style already?
